consensus_summary: Primary identification of 'week' (shabua) as a heptad of years in prophetic contexts such as Daniel 9, grounded in biblical precedents for sevens of years, with broader symbolism of divine completeness and ordered cycles drawn from the creation week and Sabbath.
book_summary: A unit of sevens (shavua) not restricted to days: Laban's 'week' equals seven years of service, the jubilee counts seven sabbaths of years, Daniel's seventy weeks are sevens of years (unpointed seventy sevens opening into seventy jubilees), and the Feast of Weeks counts seven sevens of days modeling the jubilee day-for-year.
consensus_core_identification: heptad (of years in prophetic/calendrical use) carrying completeness
book_core_identification: unit of sevens (shavua) applicable to years as well as days
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both take shavua as a heptad whose primary biblical force (Gen 29, Lev 25, Dan 9) is years rather than days. Extra consensus material on creation-week symbolism and the book's added jubilee/Feast-of-Weeks linkage and 'seventy jubilees' phrasing are non-core elaborations that do not alter the shared referent or the cases covered.
strongest_objection: Some consensus responses elevate the creation-week pattern itself as the foundational or primary sense, which the book entry simply omits.
